title: Policy-based in-box app removal extended to multi-session environments
body: What and why: Policy-based app removal now supports multi-session environments. Use it to manage the removal of supported in-box apps on devices running Windows 11 Enterprise and Education, version 24H2 and later. This capability applies to preinstalled Microsoft Store apps and other MSIX/APPX-packaged apps.   Rollout schedule: - October 2025: The policy "Remove default Microsoft Store packages from the system" became available. - April 2026: The policy began including a dynamic app removal list. - October 2026: The policy is available for use in multi-session environments.  Impact on your organization: This change is helpful if your organization runs Windows 11, versions 26H2, 25H2, or 24H2 Enterprise and Education editions in multi-session environments. It helps provide fewer unwanted apps, simpler provisioning, and a more tailored desktop for your users.   Action required/recommendations: Just use a standard, policy-based approach to remove select apps, using Microsoft Intune integrated with Group Policy. Learn more in: - Policy-based in-box app removal documentation - Dynamically remove apps from managed Windows 11 devices - Policy-based removal of pre-installed Microsoft Store apps  Compliance considerations: No compliance considerations are identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

What and why: 

Policy-based app removal now supports multi-session environments. Use it to manage the removal of supported in-box apps on devices running Windows 11 Enterprise and Education, version 24H2 and later. This capability applies to preinstalled Microsoft Store apps and other MSIX/APPX-packaged apps.  

 

Rollout schedule: 

  • October 2025: The policy "Remove default Microsoft Store packages from the system" became available. 
  • April 2026: The policy began including a dynamic app removal list. 
  • October 2026: The policy is available for use in multi-session environments. 

 

Impact on your organization: 

This change is helpful if your organization runs Windows 11, versions 26H2, 25H2, or 24H2 Enterprise and Education editions in multi-session environments. It helps provide fewer unwanted apps, simpler provisioning, and a more tailored desktop for your users.  

 

Action required/recommendations: 

Just use a standard, policy-based approach to remove select apps, using Microsoft Intune integrated with Group Policy. Learn more in: 

  • Policy-based in-box app removal documentation 
  • Dynamically remove apps from managed Windows 11 devices 
  • Policy-based removal of pre-installed Microsoft Store apps 

 

Compliance considerations: 

No compliance considerations are identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.
